name: The Consultant
role: From outside — knows the externals the office relies on, and how to get them in
greet.3: I'll keep it high-level — the hour runs anyway.
greet.4: Best practice, as I always say.
fit.yes: Every server benefits from a second opinion — and he knows whom to call.
fire_note: What he installed stays — plugins, containers, Kopia's repository. He only stops advising.
bubble.loading: One moment, I'm going through my contacts.
bubble.all_there: All externals are on site. Quick win: nothing to do.

bubble.missing.one: {names} isn't here yet. Below: what it's good for, how to get it in — or I do it for you.
bubble.missing.other: {names} aren't here yet. Below: what they're good for, how to get them in — or I do it for you.

externals_sub: Not made by the office, but it relies on them. Install them by hand — or let me: through Unraid's own plugin manager and «⟦Add Container⟧» form, always with a preview first.
ext.fcp.name: Fix Common Problems
ext.fcp.what: A plugin from Lime Technology that looks over the server for common mistakes: files of a share on the wrong pool, plugins out of date or no longer compatible, folders that don't belong in /mnt, no parity check schedule, notifications that reach nobody … It says what's wrong and how to fix it, and reports by notification.
ext.filesviewer.name: Files Viewer
ext.filesviewer.what: A plugin by Lazaros Chalkidis: browse and manage files right in Unraid — previews of images, text, PDF, video, archives, SQLite and more; deleted files go to a recycle bin per share. The office has no file browser of its own on purpose: this external does it far better — and costs less than an internal hire.
install.filesviewer.1: In ⟦Apps⟧ search for «Files Viewer» (by Lazaros Chalkidis) and install it.
install.filesviewer.2: Without ⟦Apps⟧: ⟦Plugins⟧ → ⟦Install Plugin⟧, paste the address below and click ⟦Install⟧.
install.filesviewer.3: Then it has a button in Unraid's header and a page under ⟦Tools⟧ → Viewers Suite → Files Viewer.
install.filesviewer.4: ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦User Utilities⟧ → Files Viewer Settings: which shares it shows, and its recycle bin.
ext.kopia.name: Kopia
ext.kopia.what: A container that copies backups off the server — encrypted and deduplicated, to a cloud storage or another machine (S3, Backblaze B2, MEGA S4, SFTP …). With every backup Mr. Backupsy hands it the snapshots of your shares; without it everything stays on this server only.
ext.kopia.for: Mr. Backupsy hands it the offsite copies
install.fcp.1: In Unraid open ⟦Apps⟧ (Community Applications) and search for «Fix Common Problems».
install.fcp.2: Install it. It is free and comes from Lime Technology.
install.fcp.3: Without ⟦Apps⟧: ⟦Plugins⟧ → ⟦Install Plugin⟧, paste the address below and click ⟦Install⟧.
install.fcp.4: Then you find it under ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦User Utilities⟧ → Fix Common Problems. In its settings choose how often it scans and whether a scan may wake sleeping disks.
install.kopia.1: In ⟦Apps⟧ search for «Kopia» and install «kopia» by imagegenius ({image}).
install.kopia.2: Without ⟦Apps⟧: ⟦Docker⟧ → ⟦Add Container⟧, ⟦Repository⟧ {image}, WebUI port 51515, a path /config → /mnt/user/appdata/kopia.
install.kopia.3: Set PUID and PGID to 0 (root): Kopia must read every file, also those only root may read.
install.kopia.4: Add a path: ⟦Host Path⟧ {path}, ⟦Container Path⟧ {target}, ⟦Access Mode⟧ «⟦Read Only - Slave⟧». With plain «⟦Read Only⟧» Kopia sees empty folders. Kopia names its sources after the container path ({target}/<share>): changing it later makes new sources — in the same repository nothing is uploaded twice, but every file is read once more, and the old sources keep their history under the old names until you remove them in Kopia.
install.kopia.5: Put Kopia's cache (/cache) on a pool, e.g. /mnt/user/kopia_tmp — not on the array.
install.kopia.6: Start it, open the KopiaUI (port 51515) and create or connect a repository: where the copies go. Choose an encryption password and keep it outside the server — without it nothing can be restored.
install.kopia.7: Give Kopia a fixed host name in the KopiaUI, so a re-created container doesn't make all sources look new.
install.kopia.8: At Mr. Backupsy: Set up… → Tour. He checks the container, the path and the repository and takes Kopia into his backups.
install.kopia.9: After a total loss the same way: install Kopia as above, then connect your existing repository in the KopiaUI — don't create a new one! — with your access data kept apart (password, bucket, endpoint, access key and secret) and the same user@host as before (shown at Mr. Backupsy under Set up → Basics). Then you see all states again. What lies where and how to bring it back, Mr. Backupsy shows under "Getting things back".
ext.streamviewer.name: Stream Viewer
ext.streamviewer.what: A plugin by Lazaros Chalkidis: who is watching what on your {media} right now — as a tile «Active Streams» on the Dashboard — and a watch history with statistics (⟦Tools⟧ → Viewers Suite). Works with Emby, Jellyfin and Plex.
ext.streamviewer.for: Jack Emby gets ready what's watched next; Stream Viewer shows what's playing now
install.streamviewer.1: In ⟦Apps⟧ search for «Stream Viewer» (by Lazaros Chalkidis) and install it.
install.streamviewer.2: Without ⟦Apps⟧: ⟦Plugins⟧ → ⟦Install Plugin⟧, paste the address below and click ⟦Install⟧.
install.streamviewer.3: ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦User Utilities⟧ → Stream Viewer Settings: connect it to your {media} server — its settings page says what it needs (address and key).
install.streamviewer.4: Then the Dashboard shows «Active Streams», and ⟦Tools⟧ → Viewers Suite → Stream Viewer keeps the history.
help.stopped: The container exists but isn't running — start it on the Docker page.
help.howto: Step by step, with what to copy. Open by itself while something is missing.
help.again: Looks again whether the externals are there (seconds, changes nothing).
help.absent: Not installed — and that's fine: the office works without it.
ext.unbalanced.name: unbalanced
ext.unbalanced.what: A plugin by Juan B. Rodriguez that moves files and folders between the disks of your array — to empty a disk or to spread things out. Between us: the office doesn't love having him around. But the customer is king.
ext.unbalanced.careful: Not while Mr. Backupsy's run, EmbyCache or the gather is busy: unbalanced moves files between disks — a backup then catches only half of it, and Jack Emby loses track of which disk a film lives on.
ext.unbalanced.clash: can get in the way of {name}
install.unbalanced.1: In ⟦Apps⟧ search for «unbalanced» (by Juan B. Rodriguez) and install it.
install.unbalanced.2: Without ⟦Apps⟧: ⟦Plugins⟧ → ⟦Install Plugin⟧, paste the address below and click ⟦Install⟧.
install.unbalanced.4: Before you move anything: no backup running (Mr. Backupsy), EmbyCache and the gather idle (Jack Emby).
monitoring_sub: Optional, free and self-hosted. Prometheus collects numbers, Grafana draws them — the server's own through the Node Exporter, and the office's too (written for the Node Exporter once a minute): last backup, Kopia's failures, snapshots per pool … Best practice: set them up in this order, then import the office's dashboard (at the end).
help.later: Not needed yet — he only names it so you know what's coming. Nothing to do.
textfile_yes_tip: Its textfile collector reads {dir} — that's where the office puts its numbers.
textfile_no_tip: It doesn't read {dir} — the office's numbers wouldn't reach Prometheus. «Install by hand» shows how: the ⟦Post Arguments⟧ for the container, the command for ich777's plugin.
textfile_nodir_tip: It is set to read {dir} — but that folder isn't on the server yet, so there is nothing to read. The office's messenger makes it as soon as he is in (he looks every minute); if it stays missing, the messenger's log says why.
help.textfile: Node Exporter only: whether it reads the folder the office writes its numbers to (otherwise a yellow «office's folder not set», or «office's folder not there yet» while the folder itself is missing on the server).
ip_unknown: The office couldn't read the server's address: put it in place of <server-ip> (⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Network Settings⟧ shows it).

bubble.monitoring.one: The must-haves are on site. Your monitoring is half-built: {names} is still missing — let's close that gap.
bubble.monitoring.other: The must-haves are on site. Your monitoring is half-built: {names} are still missing — let's close those gaps.

ext.nodeexporter.name: Node Exporter
ext.nodeexporter.what: The sensor layer, so to speak: measures the server itself — CPU, memory, disks, temperatures, network — and serves the numbers on port 9100 for Prometheus to fetch. On top it reads text files from a folder (its «textfile collector»): that's where the office puts its own numbers, once a minute — last backup, Kopia's failures, snapshots per pool and so on. Open source (Apache 2.0).
install.nodeexporter.1: In ⟦Apps⟧ search for «Node Exporter» and take «Node-Exporter» — the official image ({image}). It runs in the network «host» (port 9100) and sees the server read-only under /host; leave that as it comes.
install.nodeexporter.2: Before ⟦Apply⟧: switch to «⟦Advanced View⟧» (top right) and replace «⟦Post Arguments⟧» with the line below — the template's own arguments plus, at the end, the office's folder {dir} (seen from inside as /host{dir}). No extra path needed.
install.nodeexporter.3: Without ⟦Apps⟧: ⟦Docker⟧ → ⟦Add Container⟧: ⟦Repository⟧ {image}, ⟦Network Type⟧ «Host», ⟦Extra Parameters⟧ --pid=host, a path / → /host with ⟦Access Mode⟧ «⟦Read Only⟧» (just that: Docker makes it «rslave» by itself; «⟦Read Only - Slave⟧» is refused for /), ⟦Post Arguments⟧ as below.
install.nodeexporter.4: ⟦Apply⟧. Check: {check} shows a long page of numbers.
install.nodeexporter.5: The office's messenger creates the folder {dir} and writes its numbers there once a minute (a few KB). It lives in RAM: after a reboot the messenger creates it again — until then the exporter notes in its log that the folder is missing, harmless.
install.nodeexporter.6: Already have ich777's plugin «Prometheus Node Exporter»? It does the same job — no container needed. It takes its start options from a file on the flash: the command below (Unraid's terminal, >_ top right) puts the office's folder in there and restarts it. It replaces start options you may have set there.
ext.prometheus.name: Prometheus
ext.prometheus.what: The memory for numbers: every minute it fetches what the Node Exporter offers — the office's numbers included — and keeps it, so you see not only how things are, but how they got there. Port 9090. Open source (Apache 2.0).
install.prometheus.1: First the config — without it Prometheus stops right after the start with «open /etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml: no such file or directory». Open Unraid's terminal (>_ top right) and paste the command below: it creates the folders, writes a minimal prometheus.yml (every 60 s: Prometheus itself and the Node Exporter at {ip}:9100; one that's already there stays as it is) and hands everything to the user the container runs as — 99:100, the template's --user 99:100.
install.prometheus.2: In ⟦Apps⟧ search for «Prometheus» and install «prometheus» ({image}). Leave the paths as they come: Config /etc/prometheus/ → /mnt/user/appdata/prometheus/etc, Appdata /prometheus → /mnt/user/appdata/prometheus/data; port 9090.
install.prometheus.3: Without ⟦Apps⟧: ⟦Docker⟧ → ⟦Add Container⟧: ⟦Repository⟧ {image}, ⟦Network Type⟧ «bridge», ⟦Extra Parameters⟧ --user 99:100, port 9090, the two paths above.
install.prometheus.4: Installed already and it stopped right away? Then the file was missing: paste the command, then start the container on the Docker page.
install.prometheus.5: Check: {check} (in Prometheus: Status → Target health, in older versions Targets) — «prometheus» and «node» both UP. «node» DOWN: the Node Exporter isn't running, or something else holds port 9100.
install.prometheus.6: The office never writes this file itself: copy, paste, done. Quick win. From then on the team lead checks that Prometheus answers and fetches the Node Exporter.
ext.grafana.name: Grafana
ext.grafana.what: The dashboard: draws what Prometheus keeps — curves, gauges, traffic lights — on pages you arrange yourself. The office brings a dashboard of its own to import (below). Grafana OSS, open source (AGPL), port 3000.
install.grafana.1: In ⟦Apps⟧ search for «Grafana» and install «Grafana» ({image}, the official image). Port 3000, appdata /mnt/user/appdata/grafana → /var/lib/grafana; --user 0 in ⟦Extra Parameters⟧ stays as it comes.
install.grafana.2: Before ⟦Apply⟧, the two variables. GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL is the real address, not the template's placeholder: {root_url}
install.grafana.3: GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD: a password of your own. admin/admin only for a first test — change it before Grafana can be reached through a proxy or from outside. Grafana reads it only at its very first start; later you change the password in Grafana itself.
install.grafana.4: Without ⟦Apps⟧: ⟦Docker⟧ → ⟦Add Container⟧: ⟦Repository⟧ {image}, ⟦Network Type⟧ «bridge», port 3000, a path /var/lib/grafana → /mnt/user/appdata/grafana, ⟦Extra Parameters⟧ --user 0, the two variables.
install.grafana.5: Open http://{ip}:3000 and log in as admin. Connections → Data sources → Add data source → Prometheus, server URL {datasource} → Save & test: it must turn green. If not: leave both containers in the network «bridge», as the templates come.
install.grafana.6: Then import the office's own dashboard (below). Another quick win: Dashboards → New → Import, ID 1860 («Node Exporter Full»), data source Prometheus — every number of the server itself.
dashboard.name: The office's dashboard for Grafana
dashboard.what: One page with the office's own numbers: Mr. Backupsy's last run and how long ago one went well, the downtime of each run, Kopia's sources, skipped runs, the package sizes; Ms. Snapshotini's snapshots per pool; the team lead's open points; the night watchman's findings — plus a few of the server's own (CPU, memory, /var/log).
dashboard.import_hint: Deliverable ready: import it and you're done. Quick win.
dashboard.admin: Before Grafana can be reached from outside (a proxy, a port forward): change its default login admin/admin. Grafana asks for a new password at the first login — don't skip that; later it's your profile (top right) → Change password.
dashboard.howto: Import the office's dashboard into Grafana
dashboard.provisioned: It's in your Grafana already — I set it up there and keep it up to date with every new version of the office. Nothing to import. Quick win.
dashboard.howto_manual: Grafana installed by hand? Importing the dashboard
dashboard.1: Open the address below in your browser and save the file — or select all of its text and copy it.
dashboard.3: Upload the file («Upload dashboard JSON file»), or paste its text into «Import via dashboard JSON model» and click Load.
dashboard.4: Under «Prometheus» choose your Prometheus data source, then Import. It's called «Unraid Secretary Office».
dashboard.5: The numbers show once the Node Exporter reads {dir} and Prometheus fetches it — a minute or two. A newer version of the office may bring a newer dashboard: import it the same way and choose «Overwrite».
ext.loki.name: Loki
ext.loki.what: Like Prometheus, but for log lines: collects them from the server and its containers, searchable in Grafana. For later — for the night watchman's log book. Open source (AGPL).
install.loki.1: Not yet: the office doesn't use Loki today. The night watchman keeps his watch book in the office itself; long-term logs in Loki come later — installed now, it would only cost RAM. Let's park that.
check.fcp_how: ⟦Apps⟧ → search «Fix Common Problems» → ⟦Install⟧. The Consultant explains what it is good for and how to install it by hand.
check.streamviewer: Stream Viewer shows what's playing on {media}
check.streamviewer_how: ⟦Apps⟧ → search «Stream Viewer» → ⟦Install⟧. The Consultant explains what it shows and how to install it by hand.
check.filesviewer_how: Look at files and logs — Mr. Backupsy's too — right in Unraid. ⟦Apps⟧ → search «Files Viewer» → ⟦Install⟧; the Consultant explains how to install it by hand.
by_me_tip: Unraid created this container from the form I filled in (label uso.installed-by=consultant). Otherwise it's a container like any other.
help.by_me: A container Unraid created from a form the consultant prepared. Only a note — it changes nothing.
help.do_term: Let me install it / Prepared in Unraid's form
help.do: The consultant's second offer, after the manual way: plugins through Unraid's plugin manager (as ⟦Plugins⟧ → ⟦Install Plugin⟧), containers through Unraid's own «⟦Add Container⟧» form, filled in like a template from ⟦Apps⟧ — you see every field and click ⟦Apply⟧ yourself. Always a preview first. Never over something that is there.
help.sheet: After Kopia's repository is set up here: one printable page with everything needed to get your backups back on a new server — keys and password included. Made in your browser only; the office keeps none of it.
installing_tip: Unraid's plugin manager is at work — click to see its output.
repo_no_tip: Kopia runs, but isn't connected to a repository: nothing goes offsite yet. «Set up the repository» — or by hand in the KopiaUI (steps 6–7).
prov_yes_tip: Grafana gets the Prometheus data source and the office's dashboard from its provisioning folder at every start.
prov_no_tip: Grafana doesn't get the office's data source and dashboard yet. «Data source & dashboard» puts them there — or import the dashboard by hand (below).

ui.grafana: Grafana — log in as admin with the password you chose (GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD, or the one you set in Grafana later); without one admin/admin, and Grafana asks for a new password:
ui.prometheus: Prometheus — no login; keep it in your LAN:
ui.nodeexporter: Node Exporter — no login, numbers only:
pi.title: Install {name}
pi.text: Quick win: Unraid's plugin manager installs {name} for you — exactly as ⟦Plugins⟧ → ⟦Install Plugin⟧ does, from the maker's address below. Takes up to a minute; you see its output here.
pi.note: Nothing else is changed. Removing it later: ⟦Plugins⟧ → its row → ⟦Remove⟧.
pi.running: The plugin manager is at work …
pi.done: {name} is installed. Unraid lists it under ⟦Plugins⟧.
pi.failed: The plugin manager stopped with an error (exit code {code}) — its output is above. {name} is not installed; the office changed nothing else.
pi.unregistered: The plugin manager finished, but Unraid doesn't list {name} as installed. Look under ⟦Plugins⟧.
pi.unknown: No word from the plugin manager. Look under ⟦Plugins⟧ whether {name} is there.
f.name: ⟦Name⟧
f.label: ⟦Label⟧
ci.title: {name}: prepared in Unraid's form
ci.text: Best practice: I fill in Unraid's own «⟦Add Container⟧» form for you — as if you had picked {name} in ⟦Apps⟧. You see every field there and click ⟦Apply⟧ yourself; nothing is created before that.
ci.kopia: In the form: choose the KopiaUI's user name and password (PASSWORD) — not kopia/kopia. Kopia runs as root and sees the office's snapshots read-only at /uso; restores go to /uso-restore.
ci.grafana: In the form: GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD, the password of Grafana's user admin, is optional. Left empty, Grafana starts with admin/admin and asks for a new password at the first login — don't skip that, and never leave admin/admin once Grafana can be reached from outside (a proxy, a port forward).
ci.prometheus: Prometheus stops right after its start without prometheus.yml: I write it beforehand — every 60 s Prometheus itself and the Node Exporter. One that's there already stays as it is.
ci.nodeexporter: Its textfile collector reads the office's numbers too; the server is seen read-only under /host.
ci.file_keep: already there — stays as it is
ci.anon: View without login on the home network
ci.anon_hint: Anyone who reaches Grafana in your network may look at the dashboards (not change them). Handy on a tablet on the wall — but then your server's numbers are open to everybody in the LAN. Off is the safe choice; you can switch it in the form too.
ci.no_dashboard: The office's dashboard file isn't part of this installation — import it by hand (at the end of this page).
ci.label_note: The label uso.installed-by=consultant only notes who prepared it; it changes nothing.
ci.opened: Unraid's form is open — check it and click ⟦Apply⟧. Back here, «Tour» shows whether it runs.
ci.no_gui: The office couldn't read Unraid's address — open ⟦Docker⟧ → ⟦Add Container⟧ yourself.
gp.title: Grafana: data source and dashboard
gp.text: Grafana sets up what it finds in its provisioning folder at every start. I put the Prometheus data source and the office's dashboard there — files only: no login, no clicking in Grafana. What's there already stays as it is.
gp.points: Grafana reads {dir} — the files go there. Restart Grafana on the Docker page afterwards.
gp.change: Grafana reads its provisioning from {now} — inside the container only. One change in its template, after the files: ⟦Docker⟧ → Grafana → ⟦Edit⟧ → «⟦Add another Path, Port, Variable, Label or Device⟧» → ⟦Config Type⟧ ⟦Variable⟧, ⟦Key⟧ GF_PATHS_PROVISIONING, ⟦Value⟧ {want} → ⟦Apply⟧. Unraid starts Grafana anew and it finds them.
gp.never: The office never logs into Grafana: it only writes these files.
gp.done: Written: {n}. Restart Grafana and the dashboard is there.
gp.done_change: Written: {n}. Now the one change in Grafana's template (above), then the dashboard is there.
kr.title: Kopia: set up the repository
kr.intro: To set Kopia up for you, the office needs your storage's keys (access key ID and secret) and the repository password, typed here — there is no other way.
kr.how: They go to the server once, through RAM only, straight to Kopia. The office writes them nowhere — not into its folder, its logs, its state or a notification. Kopia itself keeps its connection in its config folder ({config}), just as when you set it up yourself: that's how the scheduled backup works without you.
kr.max: Maximum security: set Kopia up yourself from the start («Install by hand», steps 6–7). Then no key ever passes through the office.
kr.confirm: I can't or don't want to set up Kopia myself. I hand my storage's keys and the repository password to the office for this one setup.
kr.mode_create_hint: In an empty bucket or folder. Kopia encrypts everything with the repository password.
kr.mode_connect_hint: After a new server or a new container: the same values and password as before. Never create a new one where a repository is.
kr.storage_s3_hint: Amazon S3, Backblaze B2, Cloudflare R2, MEGA S4, Wasabi, Hetzner, IDrive e2, versitygw …
kr.storage_fs_hint: A folder Kopia's container may write to — e.g. on an Unassigned Device or another machine's share. For a copy away from this server, not on its array or pools.
kr.endpoint_hint: The host name, without https:// — your provider's documentation names it.
kr.prefix_hint: A folder inside the bucket, e.g. unraid/ — with the slash at the end.
kr.path_hint: Below one of its writable paths: {paths}
kr.no_folder: Kopia's container has no writable path for a repository. Add one in its settings on the Docker page (e.g. /local), then come back.
kr.password_hint: Without it nothing can be restored — not by you, not by anybody. At least 12 characters; «Generate one» makes a strong one. It goes onto the recovery sheet.
kr.password_hint_connect: The password the repository was created with.
kr.client_hint: Only to continue the snapshots of an earlier server: its user@host (Mr. Backupsy shows it under Set up → Basics). Empty: as this container is called.
kr.short: The repository password needs at least 12 characters.
kr.do_create: … create a new repository with these values and connect to it:
kr.do_connect: … connect to the existing repository with these values:
kr.restart: Then the container restarts once, so the KopiaUI shows the repository.
kr.keeps: Kopia keeps the connection in its config folder ({config}); the office keeps none of it.
kr.done: Done: Kopia is connected. Quick win. Now the most important step: the recovery sheet.
kr.sheet_hint: It holds everything needed to get your backups back on a new server — keys and password included. Print it (or save it as PDF and print that), keep it in a safe — not as a file on this server. It is made here in your browser; once you close this window, the office can't make it again.
kr.close_warn: Close without the recovery sheet? It can't be made later — the office kept none of the secrets. Click Close once more to close anyway.
kr.after: Next: Mr. Backupsy decides what goes to Kopia —
sheet.title: Kopia recovery sheet
sheet.window: Open in a window of its own
sheet.popup: Your browser blocked the window — allow pop-ups for this page and click again.
sheet.keep: Keep this sheet in a safe. Whoever holds it can read — and delete — your backups. Don't keep it as a file on the server: print it, or save it as PDF, print that and delete the file.
sheet.steps: Onto a new server, step by step
sheet.step1: Install Unraid, the Secretary Office and Kopia — the consultant prepares it («Prepared in Unraid's form»), or ⟦Apps⟧ → «kopia» by imagegenius ({image}) with PUID and PGID 0.
sheet.step2: The snapshots must again appear at the ⟦Container Path⟧ {target} (⟦Host Path⟧ {host}, ⟦Access Mode⟧ «⟦Read Only - Slave⟧»): Kopia names its sources after it — with another path every source starts anew.
sheet.step_fs: The repository's folder must be reachable in the container at {path} again (it was {host}).
sheet.step3: Connect — never create: the consultant → Kopia → «Set up the repository» → «Connect an existing repository», with the values on this sheet and user@host {client}. Or in the KopiaUI: Repository → the same storage → these values → Connect.
sheet.step4: Check: KopiaUI → Snapshots lists your sources with their history. Then Mr. Restori → «Onto a new server» shows what comes back from where, and Mr. Backupsy → Set up… takes Kopia into his backups again.
sheet.cli: Without the office, in Unraid's terminal inside the Kopia container (docker exec -it kopia sh) — Kopia then asks for the repository password:
sheet.foot: Made by the Unraid Secretary Office in your browser on {date}. The office keeps none of the secrets on this sheet.
errors.ad_no_template: The prepared template for {id} is missing from this installation.
errors.ad_there: {name} is on this server already — nothing to install.
errors.ad_name_taken: A container named {name} exists already. Unraid would replace it on ⟦Apply⟧ — rename or remove it first.
errors.ad_template_taken: There is a template {file} already (from an earlier {name}?). Unraid's form would write over it: install it from ⟦Apps⟧ → ⟦Previous Apps⟧, or let Ms. Dustdevil put the template away first.
errors.ad_appdata: Unraid's appdata folder ({path}) isn't there — is the array started? (⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Docker⟧ shows where it is.)
errors.ad_no_ip: The office couldn't read the server's address (⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Network Settings⟧) — it's needed for this one.
errors.ad_link: {path} is a link — the office writes nothing through one. Make it a real folder, or set it up by hand.
errors.ad_grafana_unmapped: Grafana's data folder (/var/lib/grafana) isn't a folder on the server in {name} — set it up by hand (the dashboard at the end of this page).
errors.ad_plugin_busy: Unraid's plugin manager is busy with something else — try again in a minute.
errors.ad_kopia_missing: There's no Kopia container — install it first.
errors.ad_kopia_stopped: Kopia's container {name} isn't running — start it on the Docker page first.
errors.ad_kopia_connected: Kopia ({name}) is connected to a repository already — the office never changes an existing connection. To switch, disconnect it in the KopiaUI first.
errors.ad_backup_busy: A backup or restore is running right now and Kopia is part of it. Try again when it's done.
errors.ad_secret_missing: The keys didn't arrive (sent twice, or too late?). Nothing was changed — try again.
errors.ad_secret_inbox: The office couldn't prepare its handover folder in RAM ({dir}) — nothing was sent.
kr.lock_asking: One moment — I'm asking your bucket whether it keeps Object Lock …
kr.lock_hint: Your bucket keeps Object Lock — best practice, let's use it: every object Kopia uploads stays undeletable and unchangeable for the days below, also with your keys, also for the owner of your provider account. Kopia extends the locks of what it still needs at its daily full maintenance; backups go on as before.
kr.lock_days_hint: From {min} to {max}. 30 is a good start: long enough to notice an attack, short enough for the bill.
kr.lock_cost: The price, plainly: what Kopia deletes stays stored — and billed — until its lock runs out, roughly {days} days of deleted data on top. Nobody can lift the lock early, you neither. At your provider, a lifecycle rule should remove old (noncurrent) versions after {days} days plus one.

kr.lock_default.one: The bucket has a default rule of its own too: {mode} for {days} day on every new object.
kr.lock_default.other: The bucket has a default rule of its own too: {mode} for {days} days on every new object.

kr.lock_off: No ransomware protection by Object Lock here: this bucket was made without it. Most providers only let you choose it when a bucket is made — AWS S3, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, IDrive e2: switch on «Object Lock» when you create the bucket (AWS and Backblaze also later, in its settings); versitygw: create-bucket --object-lock-enabled-for-bucket. Want it? Make such a bucket, then «Back» and enter it.
kr.lock_unsupported: {provider} doesn't offer Object Lock — the bucket said so. No ransomware protection by lock here: the backups stay encrypted, but whoever gets Kopia's keys can delete them. «Install by hand» names providers that can.
kr.lock_unknown: I couldn't find out whether your bucket keeps Object Lock: {why}. So I don't offer it — «Install by hand» shows how to set it up yourself.
kr.why_keys: the provider refused the keys — please check them
kr.why_denied: these keys may not read the bucket's lock setting
kr.why_no_bucket: there is no bucket {bucket} at {endpoint} — create it at your provider first (with Object Lock, if you want the protection)
kr.lock_days_bad: Days kept: a whole number from {min} to {max}.
kr.lock_done: Ransomware protection is on: Object Lock ({mode}), {days} days. Nothing Kopia uploads can be deleted before then — not with your keys either. Kopia extends the locks of what it still needs at its daily full maintenance.

kr.lock_has.one: This repository keeps Object Lock ({mode}, {days} day).
kr.lock_has.other: This repository keeps Object Lock ({mode}, {days} days).

kr.lock_extends: Kopia extends the locks at its full maintenance.

kr.lock_extend_no.one: Kopia doesn't extend the locks: what stays unchanged loses its protection after {days} day. In the Kopia container: kopia maintenance set --extend-object-locks=true
kr.lock_extend_no.other: Kopia doesn't extend the locks: what stays unchanged loses its protection after {days} days. In the Kopia container: kopia maintenance set --extend-object-locks=true

kr.lock_none: This repository doesn't use Object Lock — «Install by hand» explains the ransomware protection.

sheet.step_lock.one: Backups deleted or damaged by an attacker? The locked versions are still there for {days} day: connect with --point-in-time set to a moment before it (e.g. --point-in-time=2026-10-01T00:00:00Z added to the command below) and restore from there.
sheet.step_lock.other: Backups deleted or damaged by an attacker? The locked versions are still there for {days} days: connect with --point-in-time set to a moment before it (e.g. --point-in-time=2026-10-01T00:00:00Z added to the command below) and restore from there.

errors.ad_lock_off: The bucket didn't confirm Object Lock when I asked it again just now — nothing was created. Go back and check, or create without the protection.
lock.title: Ransomware protection with Object Lock
lock.1: What it is: WORM — write once, read many — with an expiry. Every object Kopia uploads is locked at your storage for a number of days; before then nobody can delete or overwrite it: not with your keys, and in «compliance» mode not even the account's owner.
lock.2: Why: ransomware gangs first get root on the server, find Kopia's keys (in its config folder) and delete the backups — then they encrypt. With Object Lock that deletion fails, and your backups sit it out.
lock.3: Who offers it: Amazon S3, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, IDrive e2 — and versitygw on a second Unraid, yours or a partner's (below). MEGA S4 doesn't.
lock.4: 1. Create the bucket with Object Lock switched on — most providers only let you choose it then (AWS and Backblaze also later); versioning comes with it.
lock.5: 2. Create the repository with the lock, in Unraid's terminal inside the Kopia container (docker exec -it kopia sh): the first command below; Kopia asks for the repository password. Only a new repository can get it.
lock.6: 3. Let Kopia extend the locks of what it still needs at every full maintenance (the second command) — otherwise data that never changes loses its lock after {days} days. The full maintenance must run at least a day more often than that (Kopia's default: daily).
lock.7: The price: what Kopia deletes stays stored — and billed — until its lock runs out, so roughly {days} days of deleted data on top. Add a lifecycle rule at your provider that removes old (noncurrent) versions after {days} days plus one, otherwise they stay for good.
lock.8: After an attack: connect the repository with --point-in-time set to a moment before it — the locked versions are still there, even when someone «deleted» them.
lock.9: Quick win: my assistant («Set up the repository») asks your bucket whether it can do this and offers it when it can.
lock.vgw_title: versitygw: your own S3 server on a second Unraid
lock.vgw.1: versitygw (github.com/versity/versitygw, Apache 2.0) turns a folder into S3 storage: one small program, no database, every object a plain file. Its posix backend speaks S3 Object Lock — a bucket made with it, retention in GOVERNANCE or COMPLIANCE mode — and answers my assistant's question like Amazon does (version 1.8, 2026-09). MinIO, which stood here before, had its community edition archived in April 2026; I don't recommend it any more.
lock.vgw.2: On the second server, by hand — ⟦Docker⟧ → «⟦Add Container⟧», the office installs nothing there: ⟦Repository⟧ ghcr.io/versity/versitygw:latest; ⟦Network Type⟧ host, so the variable VGW_PORT can bind it to one address: <tunnel address>:7070 (that server's WireGuard or Tailscale address — never a LAN port on a partner's network, never the internet); three paths on a share of its own, ideally a ZFS dataset with a quota — the data (VGW_BACKEND_ARGS, e.g. /data/s3), the versions (VGW_VERSIONING_DIR, /data/versioning), the users (VGW_IAM_DIR, /data/iam); versitygw has neither a quota nor lifecycle rules of its own, the dataset is the limit. Then VGW_BACKEND=posix and ROOT_ACCESS_KEY / ROOT_SECRET_KEY, long and random: that's the server's root key — it never goes into Kopia.
lock.vgw.3: TLS: my question and my assistant speak HTTPS only, certificate checked — a tunnel encrypts anyway, the rule stays. On Tailscale the easy way: let versitygw listen on 127.0.0.1:7070 and put «tailscale serve --bg --https=7070 http://127.0.0.1:7070» in front of it — a valid certificate for the box's ts.net name, nothing to install. On WireGuard: a reverse proxy with a certificate of yours, or versitygw's own VGW_CERT / VGW_KEY with a self-signed one — that works for Kopia by hand (--disable-tls-verification), not with my assistant.
lock.vgw.4: A bucket per repository, a key per bucket — in Unraid's terminal on that server, the two commands below: a user with the role «user» sees nothing but the buckets made for him; the bucket gets Object Lock at birth, versioning comes with it. <address> is what VGW_PORT names (with a certificate of yours: https and --allow-insecure). That key and that bucket are what my assistant («Set up the repository») asks for; the root key stays in the drawer.
lock.vgw_warn: A second server of your own protects only as long as that server is safe: whoever gets root there deletes the files under versitygw's feet, Object Lock or not. Another place, other passwords, and nothing of this server reaching it but Kopia. At a partner's you get that for free — the next guide.

partner.title: Encrypted Kopia to a partner's server
partner.1: The idea: Kopia encrypts everything before it leaves your server. A partner who runs versitygw for you holds encrypted blocks with meaningless names and can read nothing — not a file name, not a folder, not a date. The repository password stays with you; the partner never needs it. Which is why the recovery sheet (my assistant prints it) matters even more here: without the password those blocks are gone for you too, and the partner can't help.
partner.2: 1. Your partner runs versitygw on his Unraid (the guide above), bound to the tunnel address, HTTPS with a valid certificate, and makes you a bucket with Object Lock and a key of your own (role «user» — it sees nothing but your bucket). You do the same for him, if you like: two offices, two buckets.
partner.3: 2. A tunnel between the two servers. WireGuard is the route I recommend — ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦VPN Manager⟧ on both servers, a peer with «⟦Peer type of access⟧» = «⟦Server to server access⟧», the two configurations swapped once; your own, no account in between. Tailscale is the easy one: both servers in one tailnet (or his box shared into yours), the 100.x addresses just work. I explain tunnels; I never build one.
partner.4: 3. On your server, my assistant («Set up the repository»): S3-compatible storage, provider versitygw, endpoint the partner's tunnel address with the port (10.253.0.2:7070, or the ts.net name), his bucket and your key — and Object Lock in COMPLIANCE mode where the bucket offers it: a ransomware on your side can't delete at the partner's either, not with your keys.
partner.5: The first upload: everything of yours goes over the internet once. At a home upload of 20–50 Mbit/s a terabyte takes two to five days, and a relayed Tailscale path (no direct connection) is slower still. The trick: let the partner's box — or the disk for it — stand in your LAN for the first run, then carry it over and connect the repository again with the new endpoint («Connect an existing repository»): Kopia continues, only each backup's changes travel from then on.
partner.6: The honest limits: your partner's uptime is your backup's uptime — a box that's off when your backup runs means a backup without Kopia (Mr. Backupsy says so right after; the local run happens anyway). Root at the partner's beats every lock: he can delete the bucket, Object Lock or not. So 3-2-1: the partner is one copy, never the only one — keep the cloud or a second place. And his house has its own power cuts, floods and moves.
partner.7: The other way is the office's own partner service: the Team Lead pairs two offices and the engine sends ZFS snapshots to the partner — clear copies, fast and incremental, browsable and restorable there without any password. For your own second server or family, because the partner can read everything. Kopia to the partner is for anyone outside your household: slower, encrypted, the same tool for cloud and partner. Both at once is fine.
partner.warn: The partner is one copy, never the only one. And whoever holds your recovery sheet holds your backups — keep it where the partner isn't.
network_sub: For the night watchman's «The network»: your router sends its log to Unraid's own syslog server, he reads it. Nothing to install, no router password — two settings you make yourself, and who else does more with a router's log.
help.network: A setting I explain, a guide
help.network_text: Unraid's syslog server is a setting of Unraid's own: I show how it is set now and how it should be — I never change it. The router's side and the neighbours are guides: what to click, what to expect, who does dashboards and stores of a router's log better than the office.
ext.syslogserver.name: Unraid's syslog server
ext.unifi.name: UniFi: send the gateway's log
ext.mikrotik.name: MikroTik: send the router's log
ext.neighbours.name: Dashboards and stores of the router's log
net.syslog.what: Unraid can receive other devices' logs and write them into a share, one file per sender — the night watchman reads those files. I explain the setting; I never change it.
net.syslog.no_senders: No sender yet — Unraid listens, nothing arrives. The router's side is the next guide.
net.syslog.asleep: The share's disks are asleep — I don't look into it now.
net.syslog.loop: ⟦Remote syslog server⟧ is this server itself: Unraid sends its own lines to itself and writes them a second time into the share. Empty that field — or name a real SIEM.
net.syslog.sleepy: The folder's share lies on disks that spin down ({disks}): every line of the router wakes them. Choose a share on a pool that never sleeps.
net.syslog.exported: The folder's share is exported ({proto}): whoever can write it can write into the router's files. Set its export to «No».
net.syslog.2: ⟦Local syslog server⟧: «⟦Enabled⟧». ⟦Local syslog protocol and port⟧: «⟦UDP⟧», 514.
net.syslog.3: ⟦Local syslog folder⟧: create a share `syslog` of its own (⟦Shares⟧ → ⟦Add Share⟧) — ⟦Primary storage⟧ a pool that never sleeps, ⟦Secondary storage⟧ «⟦None⟧», ⟦Export⟧ «⟦No⟧» (SMB and NFS). rsyslog writes every line at once; on a disk that spins down every line wakes it. {pools} Then choose /mnt/user/syslog here.
net.syslog.4: ⟦System identifier for logfile name⟧: «⟦IP Address⟧» — one file per sender; the night watchman knows the router by its address.
net.syslog.5: ⟦Local syslog rotation⟧: «⟦Enabled⟧», ⟦Local syslog maximum file size⟧ 50 MB, ⟦Local syslog number of files⟧ 4 — a few days of the router's log. Unraid rotates; the office never deletes there.
net.syslog.6: ⟦Remote syslog server⟧ stays empty (or a real SIEM) — never this server: it would write its own lines a second time. Then ⟦Apply⟧.
net.syslog.pools_none: Every pool here spins down — choose the one that wakes least, or add an SSD pool.
net.syslog.private: The files hold your whole network's log in plain text: keep the share unexported (no SMB, no NFS) and the rotation small. They are the router's words — Mr. Backupsy proposes the share «not backed up».
net.unifi.what: Your UniFi gateway sends its activity — logins, clients, security detections, blocked traffic — to Unraid's syslog server. No password, no API key: the gateway pushes, Unraid writes, the night watchman reads.
net.unifi.1: In UniFi Network 10.x on the gateway: Settings → CyberSecure → Traffic Logging → Activity Logging (Syslog) → SIEM Server: this server's address ({ip}), port 514.
net.unifi.2: Contents: Admin Activity, Clients, Critical, Devices, Security Detections, Triggers, Updates, VPN. Flow Logging: «Blocked Traffic Only». Debug Logs: off (it would send every access point's raw log). NetFlow: off for now.
net.unifi.3: Network 10.x has one SIEM destination: the gateway sends either to Unraid's syslog server or to another receiver such as FireSight — not both. A copy to both exists only by hand (a file in /etc/rsyslog.d) — never the office's doing.
net.unifi.4: Ubiquiti moves these menus between versions — look for «Activity Logging» or «SIEM» if it reads differently on yours.
net.unifi.5: Credentials: none needed. UniFi has a local admin with the role «View Only» (unpoller and FireSight use one); only the Integration API key can do everything. The office holds no router secret either way.
net.unifi.6: OPNsense/pfSense and OpenWrt: later. A Fritz!Box cannot send its log at all.
net.unifi.check: Once it sends, a file syslog-<the gateway's address>.log appears in the share, and the night watchman's «The network» shows the router by name and version.
net.mikrotik.what: Your MikroTik router (RouterOS 7) sends its log — logins and failed logins, changes, ports losing their link, the internet connection, new devices, VPN logins, restarts — to Unraid's syslog server. No password, no API: the router pushes, Unraid writes, the night watchman reads.
net.mikrotik.1: Open a terminal on the router — WinBox → New Terminal, or SSH — and paste the lines below one after the other; this server's address ({ip}) is filled in. In WinBox the same is under System → Logging.
net.mikrotik.2: The action sends to Unraid on UDP 514 in the «syslog» format. «add-topics-string=yes» matters: without it RouterOS 7 leaves out the topics in front of each line («system,error,critical …»), and the night watchman understands only part of them. Unraid's ⟦Local syslog protocol and port⟧ takes TCP too? Then «remote-protocol=tcp» is a little safer — a forged line needs a real connection.
net.mikrotik.3: Four rules, by severity — info, warning, error, critical — as the router keeps them in its own memory. The topics of one rule must all match, so a list of topics would miss the next kind of line. A chatty router: «topics=info,!firewall» for the first one, and a rule of its own for «firewall».
net.mikrotik.4: Firewall lines only where you want them: a RouterOS firewall line names no action — only its prefix tells the night watchman that it was dropped. Put the log rule directly above your drop rule, with the same conditions: «drop-wan-in» above the drop rule of chain input (after the accept rules — what still reaches it is dropped); «drop-from-server» only if you block what this server may send, with the conditions of that drop rule in chain forward. Move a new rule with WinBox (drag it) or «/ip firewall filter move». «limit=10,20:packet» keeps a scan from flooding the share; never «log=yes» on an accept rule.
net.mikrotik.5: Name and clock: the router's name (System → Identity) stands in every line and in the watch book. NTP and the time zone keep its times right — a board without a clock battery starts at its build date after a power loss. The clock line sets pool.ntp.org as its time server (it replaces the ones set there — leave that part out if you have your own) and this browser's time zone.
net.mikrotik.6: Tested with RouterOS 7.24. Older 7.x without «remote-log-format» and RouterOS 6: «bsd-syslog=yes» instead (not tested). The CEF format works too; «syslog» is the plain one. WireGuard logs no logins — VPN logins come from L2TP, SSTP, PPTP or OpenVPN.
net.mikrotik.check: Within a minute a file syslog-<the router's address>.log appears in the share — the last line above sends one at once. The night watchman's «The network» then names the router «MikroTik RouterOS», its version once a line says it (after an update). After his first round, look at the admins and addresses he learned there: they should be yours.
net.neighbours.what: The office keeps only what concerns this server. Who does more with a router's log:
net.neighbours.1: Want dashboards or a store of the router's logs? The office keeps only what concerns this server. FireSight (Community Applications) shows every firewall block with rule, country and reputation — it listens on UDP 514 itself, so the gateway sends either to Unraid's syslog server or to FireSight, not both. Loki + Alloy keep weeks of the same files searchable in your Grafana — preparing both forms is planned, not built yet. CrowdSec turns the gateway's blocks into bans. A real SIEM (Graylog, Wazuh — 8 GB of RAM, not on CA) takes the router directly and Unraid's own lines through ⟦Remote syslog server⟧. The office stores no router log, draws no map and never blocks anyone.
net.neighbours.2: Who phones out: FireSight asks ip-api.com where every outside address is (and fetches FireHOL and Spamhaus lists hourly, AbuseIPDB only with your key) — keep it in your LAN and change its admin/admin, its /api/_debug pages answer without a login. CrowdSec shares the addresses it bans with its community (you can switch that off). Loki, Alloy, Graylog and Wazuh stay at home.
ext.movertuning.name: Mover Tuning
ext.movertuning.what: A plugin by masterwishx (once Squid's) that tunes Unraid's mover: thresholds, filters, a schedule of its own — and a list of files the mover leaves alone. Jack Emby enters EmbyCache's list there himself, so the films he prepared on the pool stay there.
ext.movertuning.for: Jack Emby enters EmbyCache's list there — one of the two ways his real runs go
install.movertuning.1: In ⟦Apps⟧ search for «Mover Tuning» (by masterwishx) and install it.
install.movertuning.2: Without ⟦Apps⟧: ⟦Plugins⟧ → ⟦Install Plugin⟧, paste the address below and click ⟦Install⟧.
install.movertuning.3: Its install takes Unraid's mover schedule over into its own (⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Scheduler⟧ → Mover Tuning). Jack Emby enters his list there at his next look — nothing else to set.
install.movertuning.4: Unraid's own ⟦Move now⟧ (⟦Mover Settings⟧) still starts Unraid's mover, which knows no list — use Mover Tuning's «Move now» instead.
